verses.text: This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, had set him free at Ramah. He had found Jeremiah bound in chains among all the captives from Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken into exile to Babylon.
The commander of the guard took Jeremiah aside and said to him, "The LORD your God announced this disaster against this place.
Now the LORD has brought it about, just as he said he would. All this has happened because you people sinned against the LORD and did not obey him.

But today I am freeing you from the chains on your wrists. If you want to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you. But if you do not want to come with me to Babylon, then do not come. Look, the whole land is in front of you. Go wherever you think is good and right."

Before Jeremiah turned to go, Nebuzaradan added, "Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has made governor over the towns of Judah. Live with him among the people. Or go anywhere else you think is right." Then the commander of the guard gave him food and a gift and let him go.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and lived with him among the people left in the land.

Some army officers and their men were still out in the countryside. They heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah son of Ahikam governor of the land, and had put him in charge of the men, women, and children, the poorest people of the land, who had not been taken into exile to Babylon.

So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah the son of the Maacathite, along with their men.

Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, made a promise to them and their men: "Do not be afraid to serve the Babylonians. Settle down in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and things will go well for you.

As for me, I will stay at Mizpah to represent you before the Babylonians who come to us. But you go ahead and harvest the wine, summer fruit, and olive oil. Store them in your jars and live in the towns you have taken over."

The Jews who were in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and all the other countries also heard that the king of Babylon had left some survivors in Judah and had made Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor over them.
So all these Jews came back to the land of Judah from all the places where they had been scattered. They came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and harvested a great amount of wine and summer fruit.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers who had been out in the countryside came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
They said to him, "Don't you know that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill you?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke privately to Gedaliah at Mizpah: "Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah. No one will know. Why should he kill you? Then all the Jews who have gathered around you would be scattered, and the survivors of Judah would be lost."
But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do such a thing! What you are saying about Ishmael is not true."
